record.paper_title: The Hidden Subgroup Problem - Review and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Exact QFT for odd cyclic groups
record.original_question: What exact quantum circuit construction, rather than only an approximation, can compute the quantum Fourier transform F_N for an odd cyclic group Z_N in time polynomial in log N?

evidence.quote: It is not currently known how to construct an exact QFT for odd cyclic groups, so this is as good as it (currently) gets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an odd integer $N \geq 3$, consider the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_N$ and its quantum Fourier transform $F_N$, the unitary operator acting on the $N$-dimensional Hilbert space with orthonormal basis $\{|x\rangle : x \in \mathbb{Z}_N\}$ defined by
$$F_N|x\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\sum_{y=0}^{N-1} e^{2\pi i x y/N}\,|y\rangle.$$
Given access to a standard universal set of one- and two-qubit quantum gates, construct an explicit quantum circuit family that implements $F_N$ exactly (rather than only up to an approximation in operator norm) on $\lceil \log_2 N\rceil$ qubits (possibly with a polynomial number of ancilla qubits), using a number of gates polynomial in $\log N$, and whose description is uniformly computable in time polynomial in $\log N$.
artifact.status_search_result: Mosca and Zalka (arXiv:quant-ph/0301093, 2003; published in Int. J. Quantum Inf. 2004) constructed an exact polynomial-size quantum circuit for the QFT over $\mathbb{Z}_N$ for arbitrary $N$, including odd $N$, using amplitude-amplification techniques. This resolves the question of an exact, rather than approximate, polynomial-time QFT for odd cyclic groups.

status_evidence.title: Exact quantum Fourier transforms and discrete logarithm algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: We show how the Quantum Fast Fourier Transform (QFFT) can be made exact for arbitrary orders (first for large primes). ... This makes Shor's discrete logarithm quantum algorithm exact.
status_evidence.claim: Mosca and Zalka give an exact polynomial-time QFT circuit for arbitrary N, including odd primes.

status_evidence.title: Exact quantum Fourier transforms and discrete logarithm algorithms (IJQI)
status_evidence.snippet: QFFT can be made exact for arbitrary orders
status_evidence.claim: Published exact construction of QFT for arbitrary N.
